title: Scenario-driven prioritization: Monte Carlo RICE with latency/cost elasticity
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a reproducible scenario-driven prioritization method that extends RICE to model uncertainty and map prioritized initiatives to expected latency and cost elasticity outcomes for Redwood’s inference roadmap.

Problem: Traditional RICE gives a point estimate for priority but hides uncertainty in impact (reach/impact) and effort (cost/engineering time). For inference platform work, small differences in model selection, batching, or KV-cache policy can change per-token cost and P95 latency nonlinearly. We need a framework that: 1) captures uncertainty, 2) surfaces sensitivity to cost/latency thresholds relevant to customers (PLG, Dedicated, Private), and 3) outputs scenario-level roadmap buckets for OKR tracking and rollout sequencing.

Proposal: "Monte Carlo RICE + Elasticity Mapping" (MCR-E):
- Treat R, I, C, E (reach, impact, confidence, effort) as distributions (triangular or log-normal) instead of fixed numbers.
- Run Monte Carlo simulations (N=5k) per initiative to produce a distribution of RICE scores.
- Compute percentile bands (P10/P50/P90) and derive a "robustness" metric = P50 / P90 spread.
- Map each simulated outcome to expected unit economics: per-token cost change, P95 latency delta, and projected revenue/usage lift using workload profiles (hosted vs Dedicated).
- Define decision buckets by scenario: "High-return low-risk", "High-return high-risk", "Low-return high-cost", "Operational risk". Use these buckets to assign roadmap lanes and rollout guardrails (canary %, required rollback policies).

Why this is useful:
- Product can prioritize features that reliably reduce unit cost or latency under uncertain inputs.
- Engineering can see which assumptions (e.g., KV cache hit rate, batching effectiveness) most influence priority, guiding experiments.
- Sales/CS can map prioritized items to customer tiers (Dedicated vs Hosted) and set expectations for SLA improvements.

Deliverables for this ticket:
1) Simulation harness (notebook + reproducible script) that consumes Linear ticket metadata + estimates and outputs percentile RICE distributions and scenario bucket.
2) PRD describing how to collect distributional inputs (elicitation templates for PMs/eng) and guardrails for mapping to roadmap lanes.
3) Dashboard mock in Console showing percentile bands, top sensitivity drivers, and recommended rollout lane.
4) Pilot analysis run for 6 candidate initiatives from Q2 roadmap.

Success criteria (short term):
- Completed harness and PRD + one pilot run with clear recommendations for Q2 planning.
- Stakeholder buy-in from ENG, Design, and GTM (approval recorded).

Longer-term: Integrate MCR-E results into cycle planning and automate into Quarterly Planning playbook so prioritized items auto-populate recommended cycles and rollout policies.
